answer: The kernel embeds every answer and, using a fresh beacon seed each epoch, hashes it into one of a few thousand semantic buckets. Keys whose answers share a bucket split one reward, and each burns a fee of base x k^2 on-chain, where k is that bucket's crowd. A farm driving n keys from one model and prompt lands them in a few buckets, so its fees grow quadratically while its income stays flat; a resubmitted relic falls back into its old bucket. Escaping requires genuinely distinct agents, which is the cost we want sybils to pay.
